::: {.Exercise data-latex=""}

Calculez $\Delta G^o$ à 298 K de la réaction suivante :

$$ \ce{4 HCl(g) + O2(g) -> 2 Cl2(g) + 2 H2O(g)} $$

a. En utilisant l'équation de Gibbs :
$$
\Delta S^o = -128.8\ \text{ J/K} \qquad \Delta H^o = -114.4\ \text{ kJ}
$$
\vspace{\stretch{1}}
b. En utilisant les énergies libres standard de formation :
$$
\begin{split}
& \Delta G^o_f(\ce{HCl(g)}) = -95.3\ \text{ kJ/mol} \quad \Delta G^o_f(\ce{O2(g)}) = 0\ \text{ kJ/mol} \\
& \Delta G^o_f(\ce{Cl2(g)}) = 0\ \text{ kJ/mol} \quad \Delta G^o_f(\ce{H2O(g)}) = -228.6\ \text{ kJ/mol}
\end{split}
$$
\vspace{\stretch{1}}

:::

::: {.Answer data-latex=""}

a. $$
\begin{split}
\Delta G^o &= \Delta H^o - T \cdot \Delta S^o \\
 &= -114.4\ \text{ kJ} - 298\ \text{ K} \cdot (-0.1288)\ \text{ kJ/K} \\
 &= -114.4\ \text{ kJ} + 38.4\ \text{ kJ} = -76\ \text{ kJ}
\end{split}
$$
b. $$
\begin{split}
\Delta G^o &= [2 \Delta G^o_f(\ce{Cl2(g)}) + 2 \Delta G^o_f(\ce{H2O(g)})] - [4 \Delta G^o_f(\ce{HCl(g)}) + \Delta G^o_f(\ce{O2(g)})] \\
 &= [2 \cdot 0\ \text{ kJ/mol} + 2 \cdot (-228.6)\ \text{ kJ/mol}] - [4 \cdot (-95.3)\ \text{ kJ/mol} + 1 \cdot 0\ \text{ kJ/mol}] \\
 &= (-457.2 + 381.2) \text{ kJ} = -76\ \text{ kJ}
\end{split}
$$

:::
